name: Sargon
overview: Sargon was a male king of Assyria, identified specifically in Isaiah 20:1. Beyond his royal status, Scripture does not provide additional personal or tribal details about him. His role as king situates him as a significant figure in the geopolitical landscape surrounding Israel during the prophetic era.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Sargon' means 'firm, faithful king; the king is legitimate,' highlighting his recognized authority and stability as a ruler. Additionally, he is referred to by the title 'King of Assyria,' which denotes his sovereignty over the Assyrian empire. Both names emphasize his established position as a powerful monarch.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Sargon beyond his identification as king of Assyria. There is no information about his tribe, lineage, or personal connections in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Sargon's mention in Isaiah 20:1 underscores his importance as a key Assyrian ruler during the time of the prophet Isaiah. His reign represents the Assyrian threat to Israel and surrounding nations, providing historical context for the prophetic messages concerning judgment and deliverance. Although details are sparse, his presence in Scripture highlights the reality of God's sovereignty over earthly kingdoms and their leaders.
